issues.t: Windshield cracks without a rock strike
issues.sym: A crack appears and spreads across the windshield, sometimes while parked or during a car wash, with no chip or impact point.
issues.why: Many owners report the Defender's windshield cracking on its own, sometimes more than once on the same vehicle. A class action has been filed over 2020-2022 models; Land Rover has not issued a recall.
issues.next: Photograph the crack and report it to the dealer and NHTSA. Ask in writing whether warranty or goodwill will cover it, and check your insurance glass coverage. A spreading crack can block your view, so replace it promptly.

issues.t: Wind noise or flapping at the windshield pillar
issues.sym: A whistle, flapping or rush of air from the windshield edge at highway speed.
issues.why: The A-pillar trim and windshield weather strip may not seal tightly, and the trim can come loose.
issues.next: Have the dealer refit or replace the A-pillar trim and seal.

issues.t: Won't restart or drops into neutral after auto stop-start
issues.sym: After the engine shuts off at a stop, it doesn't restart, or it restarts with the transmission in neutral so the SUV won't move until you reselect Drive.
issues.why: Land Rover told owners about intermittent no-restart after an eco stop-start event and sent dealers a software fix while the cause was studied.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for the stop-start software update. Until then, turning off auto stop-start each drive avoids the problem.

issues.t: Battery drain and electrical warnings
issues.sym: Battery warnings, a no-start, random electrical faults, or engine problems that the dealer traces to the battery.
issues.why: Electrical complaints are the largest group of NHTSA complaints for these model years, and dealers have linked some faults to weak 12-volt batteries.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested and ask for any software updates. A battery maintainer helps if the SUV sits.

issues.t: Key fob not detected and SUV won't start
issues.sym: The SUV won't start unless the key fob is held in one spot near the steering column.
issues.why: Owners report keyless-start detection faults that new fob batteries do not fix. Some dealers reset the system or replaced parts under a service action.
issues.next: Try the backup start position in the owner's manual. Ask the dealer about related service bulletins.

issues.t: Surround cameras or screens stop working
issues.sym: Front, rear or 360-degree cameras show nothing, or the center screen goes black.
issues.why: Owners report failed camera modules and screen blackouts. Some waited for software or parts.
issues.next: Have the dealer check for software updates and fault codes. Use mirrors and check behind you carefully until it's fixed.

issues.t: Check engine light and loss of power on early 4-cylinder
issues.sym: Check engine light, whirring noise, shaking at idle, and power so low the SUV struggles to reach 30 mph.
issues.why: Some early 2.0L Defenders needed a new turbocharger, and in one case Land Rover engineers recommended a new engine after finding it running outside its limits.
issues.next: Have it checked right away and keep repair records; repeated major repairs on a new vehicle may qualify under your state's lemon law.

issues.t: Power steering shuts off with lane assist warning
issues.sym: A 'lane assist not available' message and the steering suddenly becomes very heavy or won't turn, sometimes at start-up.
issues.why: Several owners reported to NHTSA that the power steering stopped working along with a lane-assist fault.
issues.next: Do not drive if the steering is heavy. Have it towed to a dealer and report it to NHTSA.

issues.t: Air strut leak or shock failure
issues.sym: One corner sits low, a suspension warning appears, or a knock from a broken shock.
issues.why: Owners report leaking front air struts and a broken rear shock, replaced under warranty.
issues.next: Have the suspension inspected and leaks traced while the vehicle is under warranty.

issues.t: Tail lights and brake lights can go out (recall)
issues.sym: Turn signals, brake lights or tail lights stop working, often after a bright light shines on the back of the SUV, until it's restarted.
issues.why: A voltage spike in the smoked rear light assemblies can shut them off.
issues.next: Have a dealer replace the rear lamps free under recall 21V435.

issues.t: DC-DC converter overload can cut drive power (recall)
issues.sym: Charging warnings, then possible loss of drive power or exterior lights while driving.
issues.why: On mild-hybrid models the DC-DC converter can overload under high electrical demand or fail at start-up because of software.
issues.next: Confirm with a dealer that recalls 26V248 and 26V599 are done. The software fix is free.

issues.t: Driver airbag clockspring connector can corrode (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning before a crash; the driver airbag may not deploy as designed.
issues.why: Corrosion can build up on the clockspring connector in the steering wheel.
issues.next: Have a dealer apply the free protective gel to the connector.

issues.t: Blocked cam carrier oil channel can leak oil (recall)
issues.sym: Oil leak or burning oil smell from the engine bay.
issues.why: A blocked oil passage in the cam carrier can cause an oil leak and a fire risk.
issues.next: Contact a dealer; the cam carrier is inspected and replaced if needed, free.

issues.t: Child seat belt locking may release early (recall)
issues.sym: A child seat held by the seat belt loosens or won't stay locked.
issues.why: The seat belt's automatic locking retractor can switch off too soon.
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect and replace seat belts as needed, free.

issues.t: Front seat belt pretensioners may be damaged (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash.
issues.why: The driver and front passenger belt pretensioners may be damaged and may not hold occupants properly.
issues.next: Contact a dealer; front belts are inspected and replaced if needed, free.

issues.t: Touchscreen can stay blank and hide rear camera (recall)
issues.sym: The center screen stays blank after start-up, so there is no backup camera image.
issues.why: A touchscreen software fault.
issues.next: Have a dealer install the free software update.

issues.t: Defender 130 third-row seatback may not lock (recall)
issues.sym: The third-row seatback doesn't lock firmly upright.
issues.why: The seatback latch may not engage, which weakens a child seat attached to the top tether.
issues.next: Do not use the third row for child seats until a dealer inspects it. Parts are replaced free.

issues.t: Sudden loss of drive power and power steering
issues.sym: Battery or system warnings appear, the transmission drops into neutral or park, the engine shuts off, and steering assist can be lost, leaving the SUV stranded.
issues.why: Owners of 2025 Defenders have reported these failures to NHTSA, and dealers suspected a failed DC-DC converter, with parts on backorder. Earlier model years are covered by a recall for a similar converter fault.
issues.next: Get safely off the road and call for a tow. Report it to the dealer and to NHTSA, and ask whether any new recall or bulletin covers your VIN.

issues.t: Accessory raised air intake can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: The raised air intake (snorkel) accessory feels loose or moves, and it could fall off while driving.
issues.why: The dealer-fitted raised air intake accessory (part VPLEP0543) may not have been secured properly.
issues.next: If your Defender has this accessory, have a dealer inspect and refit it free under recall 24E102.

issues.t: Engine oil leak near hot parts (recall)
issues.sym: Oil drips under the engine or a burning oil smell.
issues.why: An oil leak near the hot engine or exhaust can start a fire; Land Rover recalled about 2,000 vehicles for it (24V450).
issues.next: Contact a dealer with your VIN; the repair is free.

issues.t: Third-row seat belt anchor weld may be weak (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before a crash.
issues.why: The third-row lower seat belt anchor bracket may have a poorly welded stud, so the belt may not hold an occupant properly.
issues.next: Avoid using the third row until a dealer replaces the bracket free under recall 26V163.

issues.t: Fuel tank walls may be too thin (recall)
issues.sym: No warning; the tank could leak fuel in a crash.
issues.why: A small number of fuel tanks were made with walls that are too thin.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 26V263. A dealer will replace the fuel tank free.
